notes: CMS-specific step sequences. Every step carries a machine-readable `action` alongside the human instruction — v1 has no executor, but a later agent layer needs the action type to be data rather than prose.

new-page-aem.instruction: Raise the JIRA ticket with the brief attached and the named approver on it.
Create the page at the target AEM path, inside the correct Blueprint hierarchy (Master EN → Region → Country).
Set Page Properties: Title (10–60 chars), Meta Description (120–160 chars), Canonical, Robots tag, og:image, hreflang.
In the Author editor, add kone-container sections and give each one an ASCII-only Anchor ID.
Add Title Header XL for the H1 — one per page, and its text must differ from the Page Properties Title.
Add and configure the components named in the brief.
Set every internal link via Path Picker — never paste an author URL.
Place images from the DAM, set alt text, and configure Smart Crop (JPG/WebP, not PNG).
Preview with ?wcmmode=disabled appended to the author URL.
Run the 52-point QA checklist across all four pillars (Metadata, Content, Responsive, Accessibility & Performance).
Submit for UAT — zero S1/S2 defects before sign-off.
Activate / publish the page and re-validate on the live URL.

new-page-tridion.instruction: Raise the JIRA ticket with the brief attached and the named approver on it.
Confirm the target Structure Group exists in the publication — if it does not, the page will be invisible with no error shown.
Create the page in the correct Structure Group using the agreed Page Template.
Add the Component Presentations required by the brief and populate the RTF fields.
Populate page metadata: Title, Meta Description, Canonical.
Link Multimedia Components from the Tridion Multimedia Repository.
Preview the page in the publication before publishing.
Run the QA checklist — metadata, content accuracy, links, responsive, accessibility.
Publish to the presentation server and validate the live URL.

content-update-aem.instruction: Open the target page in AEM Sites at the path given in the brief.
Check the Blueprint / Live Copy tab — if the page inherits, confirm whether the edit should be made at master level instead.
Open the named component and apply the change exactly as specified.
If a link changed, set it via Path Picker so a relative /content path is stored.
If an image changed, reference the new DAM asset and update the alt text.
Preview with ?wcmmode=disabled and confirm the change renders as intended.
Spot-check QA Pillar 2 items on the changed section: links resolve, no /content/ leak, alt text present.
Publish the page and re-validate the live URL in Incognito to bypass the Dispatcher cache.

content-update-tridion.instruction: Open the target page in the Tridion CME at the path given in the brief.
Check whether the component is inherited from the Master publication — localize it first if a local-only change is intended.
Open the Component and apply the change; use RTF source view for HTML-level edits such as tables.
Preview the page in the publication.
Publish the page and validate on the live URL.

exf-update-aem.instruction: Open the Master EN EXF in AEM Sites → Experience Fragments.
Apply the change, setting every internal link via Path Picker.
Publish the Master EN EXF and explicitly select each child EXF — publishing the folder does NOT publish children.
Wait for the async publish to complete (20–60 seconds) before doing anything downstream.
Roll out Master EN → Region Master (AME / FPL) and wait for the rollout job to finish.
Explicitly publish the Region Master child EXFs.
Roll out Region Master → Country Sites.
Validate on live published URLs across at least three country sites, in Incognito.
Check the rendered HTML for residual /content/ paths or author domain URLs.
Validate Level 1 (Link vs Label) and Level 2 sub-links separately, and check non-English markets for un-translated labels.

seo-aem.instruction: Confirm the affected URL list and whether the issue is per-page or template-level — query-string variants are fixed at template level, not per URL.
Record the current state per URL (nofollow / noindex / canonical / metadata) so the change is evidenced.
For metadata and canonical issues, correct them in Page Properties → Basic / Advanced.
For nofollow issues, remove the attribute from internal service/tool links — internal links must never carry nofollow.
For indexation issues, apply the belt-and-braces approach: robots.txt Disallow plus a template-level noindex meta tag on thin pages.
For orphaned pages, add contextual internal links from the recommended source pages using the suggested anchor text.
Re-run QA Pillar 1 (Metadata) — 12 checks: title, meta description, canonical, robots, og:image, twitter:card, hreflang, JSON-LD, URL format.
Verify the rendered live HTML — check the tag is actually present on the published page, not just in the author config.

seo-tridion.instruction: Confirm the affected URL list and which publication each page sits in.
Record the current metadata / indexation state per URL.
Correct the metadata fields on the page or component in the CME.
Escalate template-level robots/noindex changes to Dev — they sit in the Page Template, not the page.
Publish the affected pages and validate the live rendered HTML.

bug-fix-aem.instruction: Reproduce on the stated environment using the steps in the brief; capture evidence if it is missing.
Confirm severity S1–S4 and the release impact — any S1 is a P1 Hard Block on sign-off.
Check the finding against the known bug catalogue before investigating — several of these have standing workarounds.
Inspect the rendered DOM, DevTools console, and network trace on the affected page.
Apply the fix or the documented workaround in the CMS; escalate to Dev if it is template- or code-level.
Re-test on the same environment with the original reproduction steps.
Check the same component on at least two other pages/markets for the same defect.
Promote through the environment gates — DEV→QA needs zero S1/S2, QA→PRE-PROD needs UAT sign-off.

bug-fix-tridion.instruction: Reproduce on the stated environment using the steps in the brief; capture evidence if it is missing.
Confirm severity S1–S4 and release impact.
Check whether the defect comes from the Master publication — if so, fix at master rather than per market.
Apply the fix in the CME, or escalate template/schema-level issues to Dev.
Re-test and publish, then validate the live URL.

migration-aem.instruction: Open the source Tridion page and inventory every component, asset and link on it.
Audit the retrofitting / migration spreadsheet for duplicate rows before executing — duplicates create the wrong page.
Confirm the Tridion → AEM component mapping for every component on the source page.
Create the AEM page at the target path, inside the correct Blueprint hierarchy.
Set Page Properties from the SEO mapping sheet — Title, Meta Description, and the canonical that matches the new live URL.
Rebuild the page structure as kone-container sections with ASCII-only Anchor IDs.
Move content into the mapped AEM components; convert pipe-delimited or RTF tables to the inline-styled HTML table standard.
Re-point images to DAM assets (JPG/WebP for Smart Crop) and carry over or write alt text.
Rebuild every internal link with Path Picker — do not carry across legacy absolute URLs.
Verify the parent/child position in AEM Sites so breadcrumbs render correctly.
Confirm the 301 from the legacy URL and the canonical both match the SEO mapping sheet.
Run the 8-section AEM Migration QA checklist, ending on both Preview mode and the live published URL.
Publish the page once UAT is signed off with zero S1/S2.

rollout-aem.instruction: Author and publish the Master EN pages/EXFs first.
Explicitly publish EACH child EXF — a folder publish silently skips them.
Roll out Master EN → Region Master (AME / FPL).
Wait for the async rollout job to complete (20–60 seconds) before triggering anything downstream.
Explicitly publish the Region Master EXF children.
Roll out Region Master → Country Sites.
Publish the Country Site pages and EXFs.
Validate the live published URLs in Incognito to bypass the Dispatcher cache.
Confirm no raw /content/ paths in the published HTML, and that every region named in the brief is covered.

blueprint-adoption-aem.instruction: Confirm the market list and split into one ticket per market — bundling breaches One-Ticket-Per-Market.
Run the Content Readiness Checklist: copy, images, metadata and links all validated before build starts.
Publish the source Master EN page.
Roll out Master EN → Region Master and wait for the async job.
Roll out Region Master → the target country sites.
Where the market needs a local variation, localize only the affected sections — everything else stays inherited.
Apply translations per the localization scope and check for English strings left in navigation or hardcoded labels.
Route to the named local approver in each market — the 3-day SLA runs per market.
Publish the country pages and validate each live URL.

blueprint-adoption-tridion.instruction: Confirm the market list and split into one ticket per market.
Verify the Structure Group exists in every child publication — if missing, the page is invisible with no error shown.
Push the Master content down the Blueprint chain to the child publications.
Localize only where the market needs a variation; use Undo-Localize to re-sync a market with global.
Apply translations per the localization scope.
Route to the named local approver in each market.
Publish per publication and validate each live URL.

qa-audit-aem.instruction: Confirm the page/component/region list and the environment to audit.
Pillar 1 — Page Properties & Metadata (12 checks): title, meta description, canonical, robots, og:image, twitter:card, hreflang, JSON-LD, URL format.

Pillar 2 — Content & Components (19 checks, highest priority): single H1, broken internal links, raw /content/ paths, author domain leaks, 404 CTAs, missing alt text, modern image formats, width/height attributes.
Pillar 3 — Responsive Layout (8 checks): 375px / 768px / 1440px breakpoints, touch targets ≥ 44px, no horizontal overflow.
Pillar 4 — Accessibility & Performance (13 checks): skip links, form labels, autocomplete, HTTPS, cookie consent, TTFB, response size, WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA.
Raise each finding with severity S1–S4 and evidence attached.
Apply the promotion gates: DEV→QA zero S1/S2; QA→PRE-PROD UAT sign-off and zero S1/S2/S3; PRE-PROD→PROD LCP ≤ 2.5s, CLS ≤ 0.1, INP ≤ 200ms, WCAG AA.
Sign off only after verifying on both Preview mode and the live published URL, in Incognito.
